profile.name: Alex
profile.bio: 200L Computer Science student. A fictional character for this exercise.

items.misuse: Dates of birth are often used to verify identity or answer security questions, and help someone guess passwords.
items.safer: Celebrate in a private chat, or share the day and month only with a limited audience.

items.text: Photos of the hostel room, showing the gate, block and room number on the door.
items.misuse: A stranger could work out exactly where to find Alex or which room to target.
items.safer: Avoid showing door numbers, gate signs or street names. Crop or blur them.

items.text: 📍 Live location tag: at the study centre right now, alone, until late.
items.misuse: Live location shows when Alex is alone and where, which can enable stalking or targeting.
items.safer: Post after you have left, or share location only with trusted friends.

items.text: Phone: 080X XXX XXXX (public on the profile)
items.misuse: It can be scraped for spam, scam calls, SIM-swap attempts or account recovery abuse.
items.safer: Keep it out of public bios. Share it directly with people who need it.

items.text: ✈️ Travelling home Friday. Hostel empty for two weeks!
items.exposes: When the room will be unoccupied.
items.misuse: Burglars can use it to know when nobody is around.
items.safer: Share holiday photos after returning, and tell only people who need to know.

items.text: Daily routine: gym 6am, lectures 8am, library till 10pm. Every single day!
items.misuse: Someone could predict where Alex will be and when, especially combined with location tags.
items.safer: Keep routines general and avoid posting exact times and places.

items.text: Profile photo: Alex smiling at a coding club event.
items.why: A normal profile photo with no location detail, ID or address. Low risk on its own.

items.text: Congratulating a coursemate on finishing exams.
items.why: Positive, general and reveals nothing sensitive. Low risk.

items.text: Opinion about a favourite football team.
items.why: A harmless interest. Public does not automatically mean risky.

items.text: Shared a first web app project on a coding page.
items.why: Builds a positive online reputation. Just avoid sharing secret keys or personal data in the project.

lesson.b: What you deliberately share: posts, comments, photos, sign-ups.
What is collected about you: location data, device details, browsing history, tags by other people.
Private audiences reduce exposure but are not secret. Friends can screenshot or forward.
Photos and check-ins can reveal where you live, study and travel. Turn off location tags where not needed.
Employers, supervisors and others may look you up. Think about how a post will read in years.
Once posted, content can be copied, screenshotted or archived. Deleting helps but does not guarantee removal.
A public detail is not automatically an incident. Risk depends on what details combine, who can see them and why.
